name: Nuclear plant safety
summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on one power line as strikes on Ukraine's grid continue
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its last off-site line on 20 Aug, its 26th such loss, and ran on diesel for about 18 days until an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire allowed repairs (ANS). It still depends on a single 330kV line while Russian strikes on Ukraine's grid continue (1 Nov). Trump has raised further bombing of Iranian nuclear sites (Al Jazeera, 1 Nov).
for_you: No radiological release has been reported. Official guidance in an emergency would come from the IAEA and national authorities.
rubric_hit: IAEA-reported loss of all off-site power (Aug–Sep); plant still on one line

sources.title: ANS Nuclear Newswire — Zaporizhzhia restores off-site power following IAEA-brokered local ceasefire
Pakistan Today (Reuters) — Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands in Ukraine
Al Jazeera — Iran and US explore diplomacy amid rising threats of war

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
